curriculum.lesson_evidence: Natural environments can be grouped by features such as climate, vegetation and landforms (desert, rainforest, grassland, coast, alpine). Australia contains many types.

lesson.child_mission: Natural environments can be grouped by features such as climate, vegetation and landforms (desert, rainforest, grassland, coast, alpine). Australia contains many types.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same HSIE idea to a new place or source, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Match features to type: few trees, very low rainfall; tall dense trees, high rainfall; waves, dunes, salt spray.

FEEDBACK
Desert; rainforest; coast.

WATCH FOR
Calling every green place a rainforest ignores grasslands and managed parks.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Sort twelve environment cards into types with two feature reasons each. Sketch an Australia outline showing at least four environment types from an atlas.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Natural environments can be grouped by features such as climate, vegetation and landforms (desert, rainforest, grassland, coast, alpine). Australia contains many types.
materials: Optional: local map, photo or interview notes
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
